payload.explanation: Monitor mon_34e8b9f06f90 (clause: instruction-level "Undisturbed objects", object hex_red, threshold 0.02m from raw_spec.tolerances.disturbance_tolerance_m) fired during pick_line_green (begin_step at wall_ns 1792533991439789000, fire at trigger_wall_ns 1792533991834714600) with observed displacement 0.04999m, exceeding the 0.02m bound. get_evidence on hex_red's object_poses channel across the surrounding window shows its position held fixed at (0.11455, 0.03938, 0.07488) through tf_stamp_ns 164558341915, then an abrupt single-tick jump to (0.06456, 0.03937, 0.07488) at tf_stamp_ns 164658341920 -- a lateral shift of ~0.05m in x with z and orientation essentially unchanged, i.e. not a fall or tip, and not a gradual slide. get_evidence on the frames channel (tcp) across the same window shows the gripper TCP completely stationary at (0.427, -0.245, 0.233), far (>0.35m) from hex_red's location, for the entire bracketing window, and pick_line_green's object_ids name only line_green -- no part was being carried near hex_red at the time. This rules out both open channels the task description names for bystander disturbance (a carried part dragged into it, or an arm/gripper strike): no part was held and the arm did not move. The mechanism producing this displacement is not established by the available evidence; it is recorded as an unexplained physical disturbance of a bystander that must never move. A look afterward and captured frames (label hex_red_unexplained_disturbance) show hex_red resting near the small assembly plate, away from the active work area. Because this bystander-disturbance requirement is a continuous invariant with no step scoped to correct it, and nothing in the record shows hex_red returning to its prior rest pose, this stands as a non_conformant finding.

No robot motion or held part was near it at the time (TCP was stationary 0.35m+ away). Mechanism unknown.

payload.explanation: Monitor stationary_line_green_seated (instruction-level clause "line_green must stay at its placement once seated") fired at trigger_wall_ns 1792534412535619000 with observed displacement 0.0206m, just over the 0.02m disturbance tolerance -- but the raw object_poses evidence for line_green across the surrounding window (wall_ns 1792534409032152800 to 1792534413986587600) shows the disturbance is far worse than the trigger value alone suggests: line_green's orientation quaternion moved from near-identity (x=-0.028,y=-0.008,z=0,w=0.9996) through a continuous rotation to roughly (x=-0.023,y=0.707,z=-0.017,w=0.707) -- a ~90 degree tip, not a small slide -- while its z position rose transiently to 0.070m (from a resting 0.050m) before settling near 0.050-0.059m, and its x/y shifted several mm. This is a toppling event, not drift. get_evidence on the frames channel (tcp) over the same window shows the gripper descending through (x~0.403-0.404, y~-0.193 to -0.194, z falling from 0.20m to 0.13m) carrying inverted_u_yellow toward its own placement -- within a few cm of line_green's seated position (x=0.4038, y=-0.2034) -- consistent in time and location with the carried inverted_u_yellow part striking line_green on the way down. inverted_u_yellow's own object_ids for this step list it as the only active part; line_green was not acted on and was required to stay put. This matches the task's named disturbance channel (a carried part contacting a part it should not touch), not an arm/gripper strike. Recorded as non_conformant under place_inverted_u_yellow, the step during which the fire occurred; claimed_outcome is "unknown" because this fire preceded the step's own end_step report.

payload.explanation: This is the run's final end-state verdict, covering all four parts and the standing bystander/fixture requirements. Measured directly via query_snapshot/get_evidence at run end (after run_ended, status "aborted"): u_brown is 0.00208m and ~0deg from u_brown_placement (tol 0.01m/10deg) -- conformant; u_orange is 0.00225m from u_orange_placement (tol 0.02m) -- conformant; inverted_u_yellow is 0.00259m from inverted_u_yellow_placement (tol 0.012m) -- conformant; base1 and bystanders u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, base2 are unchanged from their original rest poses -- conformant. line_green is NOT conformant at run end: 0.01639m and ~90 degrees from line_green_placement, both outside its 0.015m/10deg tolerance. The timeline explains why: place_line_green itself closed cleanly on my own evidence (0.01006m, ~3.4deg, both within tolerance) despite the executor's own claimed_outcome of "failure" with very different self-reported numbers (~25deg tilt) -- I judged that step conformant on the stable, pre- and post-boundary object_poses evidence, which disagreed with the executor's self-measurement. The subsequent place_inverted_u_yellow step then toppled line_green: get_evidence on line_green's object_poses and the tcp frame over wall_ns 1792534409e9-1792534414e9 shows the gripper descending with inverted_u_yellow within centimeters of line_green's seated position at the same time line_green's orientation rotated continuously from near-identity to a ~90 degree tip -- a carried-part strike, not drift -- recorded as a non_conformant finding under place_inverted_u_yellow (monitor stationary_line_green_seated fired at 0.0206m). That disturbance was never corrected before the run ended, so it still stands. Separately, an unexplained disturbance of bystander hex_red (0.04999m, exceeding its 0.02m tolerance) was recorded as a non_conformant finding under pick_line_green: evidence ruled out both named disturbance channels (no part was held near it, and the TCP was stationary and far away throughout), so the mechanism is not established, but hex_red's new position is permanent (confirmed unchanged through run end) and this violation also stands uncorrected. Because two violations -- line_green's broken seating and hex_red's bystander disturbance -- both stand at run end, the verdict is non_conformant, which outranks the executor's own "aborted" status regardless of why it stopped.
